title: Bounded comparison with four previously transcribed railway corridor strings

reproducibility.time_policy: Fixed review date from input; no wall-clock timestamp

provenance.route_source_note: The four strings below were read from the frozen-corridor tables in two recovered project reviews dated 21 August 2026. They have not been freshly transcribed from the retained map photographs or validated as an operational 1948 network.

provenance.retained_map_context: The project holds photographs of a South Australian railways map dated 30 June 1938; this is not itself proof of service availability in November 1948.
provenance.transcription_note: Physical line 2, MLIAOI, is treated separately as cancelled, as in the recovered route-hypothesis review. Physical lines 1, 3, 4 and 5 are active. This freezes a reading for a sensitivity test; it does not settle the identity of ambiguous marks or the meaning of the writing. The first characters of physical lines 1 and 3 vary independently between W and M; only the terminal character of physical line 4 varies between C and S.

method.comparison: Each active code line compared separately with each corridor in both directions
method.matching: Exact, contiguous character matching; no gaps, skipped initials, substitutions or reordering
method.full_line_match: The complete code line occurs as a contiguous substring of the oriented corridor string
method.longest_overlap: Longest common contiguous substring; all tied matching positions retained
method.line_boundaries: No matches may cross code-line boundaries
method.cancelled_line_policy: Compared separately once against each corridor in both directions; excluded from all active-line aggregates
method.positions: Zero-based starts, with separate displayed one-based character positions
method.statistical_significance: Not calculated: no null model or full-network search was performed

caveats: The tested universe comprises four supplied strings, not all railway routes and not a reconstructed 1948 multimodal network.
The corridor strings are previous transcriptions. Their station completeness, ordering, naming dates and operational status have not been freshly verified for this test.
The corridor names are labels inherited from the supplied transcriptions; their use does not establish that every named endpoint existed or was served in 1948.
A zero full-line match rejects only an exact contiguous match within these strings under the tested readings. It does not refute all place-initial itineraries.
A short shared substring is descriptive overlap, not evidence of a journey or statistical significance.
The C/S comparison tests sensitivity to a proposed character reading. It does not identify Adelaide Quarantine Station or establish AQS as a period abbreviation.
This test contains no journey times, fares, transfers, ferry access, personal movements, motive or proof of authorship.

summary.interpretation: Descriptive exact-string comparison limited to the four supplied prior corridor transcriptions; no conclusion about all possible itineraries or the full 1948 network follows.
